evolution is not necessarily a process that occurs in the population as a single whole.

The main takeaway from our work is that

evolution can be endless, not only in terms of changes in the properties (e.g. mean values) of a population over many generations but also in terms of the dynamics of the lineages of individuals along their lines of ancestry, even in the presence of an apparently stationary population.
the notion of evolution as a process of changes in the properties (or the mean values) of a population may not exhaust the possibilities of evolution.

evolution can occur in an endless fashion even in the stationary population, and that the notion of the evolution of a population should be broadened to include the dynamics of lineages within the population.
